question: A researcher notices that colleagues' very long chats keep running smoothly, while hers stops making room for new content once it fills up. What is the most likely explanation?
options: A) Automatic context management is unavailable to her because her plan does not include the Artifacts feature.
B) Automatic context management is unavailable to her because code execution is not switched on in settings.
C) Automatic context management is unavailable to her because web search has not been enabled for the chat.
D) Automatic context management is unavailable to her because she has too many documents inside a Project.
correct_answers: B) Automatic context management is unavailable to her because code execution is not switched on in settings.
explanations: Incorrect. Artifacts are an output format and are widely available; they have no bearing on context management.
Correct. Code execution must be enabled for automatic context management to work, so without it a conversation simply runs out of room.
Incorrect. Web search affects what Claude can look up, not whether earlier messages can be condensed.
Incorrect. The size of a project's knowledge base does not govern whether a conversation can condense itself.
